rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Antigens and antibodies, immune response ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Antigens and antibodies** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Human Health and Diseases fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  An **antigen** is any substance that the immune system recognises as foreign and reacts against (toxin, protein on a pathogen surface, pollen). An **antibody (immunoglobulin)** is the Y-shaped protein a plasma B cell secretes to bind that antigen specifically. Antibodies never kill directly — they tag: neutralise toxins, coat pathogens for phagocytes (opsonisation), clump them (agglutination), or trigger complement.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Antigen = foreign molecule binding antibody/MHC; antibody = Y-shaped Ig (2 heavy + 2 light chains, disulphide bonds) with variable antigen-binding sites — draw the Y.  ·  Trick 2: Ig classes: IgG (most abundant, crosses placenta), IgA (secretions), IgM (first response, pentamer), IgE (allergy), IgD — the five classes with one role each.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) Draw and label the Y-shaped antibody (heavy, light, variable, constant). (2) Match the five immunoglobulin classes to their locations and roles. (3) Compare primary and secondary response (lag, magnitude, antibody class). (4) Active vs passive immunity with one example each.…  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Antigens trigger clonal selection; antibodies are specific Y-shaped tags with five classes (GAMED) each suited to a compartment and a job. The primary response is slow IgM; the secondary is fast massive IgG from memory cells. **Self-check:** can you sketch the antibody and name which class responds first?
